bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets criminal-history look-back periods, income tests, or rules for using credit or eviction reports in tenant screening, and none protects applicants because of a housing voucher or other source of income. The West Virginia Fair Housing Act bars refusing to rent, setting different terms, or advertising a preference because of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex, familial status, blindness, disability or national origin. It does not bar refusing a person convicted of illegally manufacturing or distributing a controlled substance, and it does not require renting to a person whose tenancy would be a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage to others' property (you must prove it). An owner-occupied rooming house with no more than four rented rooms is largely exempt, and some small owners are exempt as to familial status only. No West Virginia statute bars or requires asking an applicant for a Social Security number; if you ask, ask every applicant the same way (national origin is a protected class), and if you keep Social Security numbers electronically, the data-breach notice duties apply (see Tenant Information and Data Breaches). Apply written criteria to every applicant the same way.

title: Foreign Owners and Tenants
bodyText: A 2025 West Virginia law, in effect since July 10, 2025, bars a prohibited foreign-party-controlled business from acquiring or owning, directly or indirectly, any interest in West Virginia real estate, and bars anyone from holding such an interest as its agent, trustee or fiduciary; the Attorney General can force a judicial sale. A prohibited foreign party includes a citizen or resident of the People's Republic of China who is not a U.S. citizen or resident alien, that government, entities they significantly control, and any government, entity or person a majority of six named state officials identifies as hostile; a business is covered if such a party owns or operates, even in part, a controlling interest (50 percent or more). The law does not say whether leasing a home to such a business gives it an interest in real estate, and it does not restrict individual foreign tenants. A person not subject to the law need not investigate whether another party is. Otherwise any alien may own land in West Virginia as if a citizen.

title: Refusing a Service or Assistance Animal
bodyText: Apart from the White Cane law described below, which may reach a rooming house, no West Virginia statute makes it a crime to refuse an assistance animal in a tenant's home; refusals are handled under the West Virginia Fair Housing Act. A request for an assistance animal (a service, therapy or support animal under 150 pounds) may not be unreasonably denied or delayed, or conditioned on a fee, deposit or pet terms. You may ask for documentation of the disability-related need, and you may deny the animal itself if there is credible evidence, based on an individualized assessment of the specific animal's actual conduct, that it poses a direct threat to others' health or safety or would cause substantial physical damage to others' property that another reasonable accommodation cannot fix. A tenant can sue for actual and punitive damages and attorney's fees; in an administrative case civil penalties can reach $10,000 for a first violation ($25,000 and $50,000 for repeat violators), and in an Attorney General case up to $50,000 for a first violation and $100,000 after. Separately, the state's White Cane law makes it a misdemeanor (fine up to $50) to deny a person with a disability accompanied by a service animal admittance to hotels, lodging places and other places open to the public, which may reach a rooming house or a leasing office, and falsely representing an animal as a service animal to obtain those rights is also a misdemeanor.

title: Plain Language Leases
bodyText: A written residential lease must be written in a clear and coherent manner using words with common and everyday meanings, printed in type of an easily readable size with ink that contrasts with the paper, and organized and captioned by section so it is easily understood. This applies to agreements entered into after April 1, 1982, for the rental of space to be occupied for residential purposes. A violation does not make the lease void or voidable, but if the tenant asks (at signing or later) for the lease to be rewritten to conform and you refuse, the tenant can sue to have it reformed, and the tenant cannot waive this right. Words a state or federal law requires or permits may be used. No statute sets a minimum point size or requires a statement listing the rights the tenant gives up.

title: Electronic Leases and Records
bodyText:
West Virginia's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act lets you sign leases and keep records electronically, but only with a tenant who has agreed to do business electronically (agreement can be shown by the circumstances and conduct), and a party who agreed may still refuse to do a later transaction electronically; that right cannot be waived. An electronic record satisfies a law requiring a writing, and an electronic signature satisfies a law requiring a signature.

Where a law requires you to give the tenant information in writing, an electronic version counts only if the tenant can keep it when it arrives, and a record the tenant cannot print or store is not enforceable against the tenant; consumer-consent rules may also apply, including telling the tenant beforehand about the right to paper copies and to withdraw consent. Notices of default, eviction or the right to cure under a rental agreement for an individual's primary residence are excluded from the Act, so give those on paper.

title: Delivering Notices
bodyText:
West Virginia has no general rule for delivering landlord-tenant notices; each statute sets its own method, and this library's Notices clause defers to those methods rather than replacing them. A notice ending a year-to-year tenancy must be in writing; for a shorter periodic tenancy the statute calls for "like notice" or notice for one full period, which is best read as written notice too, so give it in writing. Either way, yours may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding the premises under the tenant, and the tenant's on any owner or the owner's agent.

To recover possession of abandoned property you post a written notice on the property; to dispose of belongings you also mail notice first-class with a certificate of mailing, in an envelope marked "Please Forward", to the property, any known post office box and any forwarding address. The deposit refund and itemization may be delivered personally or mailed to the tenant's last known or forwarding address. An eviction hearing notice is served under the civil procedure rules or by certified mail, return receipt requested.

Default, eviction and right-to-cure notices for a primary residence are outside the electronic transactions act, so deliver them on paper; other notices may go by e-mail only if both sides agreed to deal electronically and no statute requires a particular method, such as posting or mail. If you know an electronic notice did not reach the tenant, try again at another e-mail or the postal address on file.

title: Written Leases and Long Terms
bodyText: A lease of land for more than one year is not enforceable unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged or that party's agent, and no action may be brought on any agreement that is not to be performed within a year unless it is in a signed writing. A lease for a term of more than five years must be created by deed, and once recorded (or a memorandum of it is recorded) it is valid against the landlord's creditors and buyers. Oral leases are still rental agreements under the deposit law, and without a written lease a landlord can still recover reasonable payment for the use and occupation of the property. Electronic records and signatures satisfy these rules when both sides agreed to deal electronically.

title: Statutory and Court Forms
bodyText: West Virginia's Code gives an optional short form for a deed of lease (it may be used "or to the same effect") and the forms of an order of attachment for rent; it prescribes no form for a residential lease, a notice to quit or a nonpayment notice. The abandonment notice for disposing of a tenant's belongings has required contents but no set form. For an eviction, the courts publish magistrate court forms: the Petition for Summary Relief for Wrongful Occupation of Residential Rental Property (MLTPTWR), the Civil Summons (MLTSMWO) and the tenant's Answer (MLTAWWO). The petition form tells both sides that a jury must be requested in writing within 5 days after service.

title: Blank Spaces in the Lease
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires every blank in a residential lease to be filled in before signing. Fill every blank anyway: the late-charge, nonrefundable-fee and utility-billing rules depend on what the written agreement says. For copies of the signed lease, see Copy of the Lease.

title: Required Lease Contents
bodyText: West Virginia has no list of terms a residential lease must contain; a list exists only for factory-built home site rentals. A written residential lease must be in plain language, and some rules take effect only if the lease provides for them (see Where West Virginia Law Lets Your Lease Decide). A lease of a unit in a condominium under the Unit Property Act must state the name of the property and the unit designation (see the Condominium or Community Unit clause), and a lease of 20 years or more, counting renewal options, of a unit in a common interest community triggers the association resale certificate.

title: Where West Virginia Law Lets Your Lease Decide
bodyText: Several West Virginia rules apply only if, or unless, the lease says so. You may take late charges from the security deposit only if they are reasonable and specified in the rental agreement, and other damages or charges only as the rental agreement provides. A pet fee or application fee is outside the deposit rules only if you and the tenant expressly agree in writing that it is nonrefundable. The deposit law's definitions say you may use submetering, energy allocation equipment or a ratio utility billing system if the rental agreement so provides, so put any such arrangement in the lease. Rent is reasonably reduced after a fire or other casualty unless the lease otherwise provides, and rent ends or is reduced when land is taken by eminent domain unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. The statutory notice periods for ending a periodic tenancy do not apply where a special agreement fixes another notice period or none. A lease that gives you greater repair duties than the habitability statute controls. Terms waiving deposit rights or a deceased tenant's estate's right to end the lease are unenforceable or void (see Lease Terms West Virginia Voids).

title: Landlord Registration
bodyText: West Virginia has no statewide landlord or rental registration or licensing requirement. Cities may by ordinance set up a registration, with fees, for buildings found uninhabitable under the local building code and a registration and maintenance program for vacant buildings. A statute in the Municipal Home Rule Program section also says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals, and may regulate activities that arise from rental use only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not. Whether that reaches every city, and whether it rules out a registration or inspection ordinance that applies only to rentals, is unsettled. Ask the city or county where the property is located. Business filings with the Secretary of State are separate from landlord registration but can matter to a landlord. An out-of-state LLC that owns income-producing real property in West Virginia is transacting business here and may not maintain an eviction or other action until it obtains a certificate of authority. Anyone who rents under a name other than their own, or other than their entity's registered name, must first file that name, and willfully failing to is a misdemeanor (W. Va. Code §§ 31B-10-1003(b), 31B-10-1008(a), 47-8-2, 47-8-4, 47-8-5; see "Out-of-State Landlords").

title: Selling the Property or Changing Managers
bodyText: When rented property is sold, inherited or assigned, the new owner can enforce the lease's conditions and covenants as you could, and the tenant has the same benefit of the lease's conditions, covenants and promises against the new owner as against you (except any warranty); the transfer is effective without the tenant's attornment (acknowledgment). A tenant who pays rent to you before notice of the transfer is protected, so give the tenant written notice of the sale and where to pay. Whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends must return any deposit owed, whether or not the deposit was handed over. No statute says when the seller's own liability ends or requires notice of a change of manager, but a managing agent who does not disclose the owner's name is treated as the landlord under the deposit law. Converting a rental building to a condominium or other common interest community gives residential tenants 120 days' notice and a 60-day option to buy, and a buyer at a trustee's sale under a deed of trust has its own notice rules (see Tenants After a Trustee's Sale).

title: Owner and Manager Identity
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to give the tenant the owner's or manager's name and address. But a managing agent who does not disclose the name of the owner or lessor is treated as the landlord under the security deposit law, and if the Consumer Credit and Protection Act's debt collection rules reach rent (not settled), failing to clearly disclose the name and full business address of the person the debt is owed to when demanding payment is a prohibited practice. Put the owner's or manager's name and an address for notices in the lease.

title: Automatic Renewal
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates automatic renewal clauses in residential leases. Without one, a lease for a fixed term ends on its end date with no notice needed; a year-to-year tenancy ends on written notice at least three months before the end of a year; and a shorter periodic tenancy ends on like notice or on notice of one full period before the end of a period (give it in writing). A special agreement in the lease can fix another notice period or none. Some rules turn on when a lease is entered into or renewed (for example, a deceased tenant's estate may end a lease entered into or renewed on or after July 1, 2012), so treat each renewal as a new lease date. West Virginia's subscription-cancellation statute covers correspondence courses, occupational courses and magazine subscriptions, not leases.

title: Claims Against the Property
bodyText: If someone other than you claims the property or the rent, a tenant's attornment to that stranger (agreeing to hold the property under them or pay them rent) is void unless you consent or it is under a court's judgment, order or decree. No West Virginia statute requires a tenant to tell you about a lawsuit, foreclosure or other claim against the property; only a lease term can require that. When you transfer the property, the transfer is effective without the tenant's attornment, and a tenant who paid you before notice of the transfer is protected.

title: Mediation and Arbitration
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires mediation, arbitration or a pre-suit meeting before a landlord-tenant case. Under West Virginia's Revised Uniform Arbitration Act, an agreement in a record made on or after July 1, 2015 to arbitrate existing or future disputes is valid, enforceable and irrevocable except on grounds for revoking any contract; a court that orders arbitration must stay a related court case; and some of the Act's protections, such as the right to be represented by a lawyer, cannot be waived before a dispute arises. Whether an arbitration clause can stop a residential eviction case, or is enforceable in a residential lease at all, is case law. The library offers an optional arbitration clause for money disputes that keeps eviction cases in court (see Binding Arbitration in a Lease); it does not offer a mediation clause.

title: Lease Translation
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential lease to be translated, even when it is negotiated in another language. The lease must be in clear and coherent words with common and everyday meanings, and in statutes for other transactions a party's inability to understand the language of an agreement is a factor in deciding whether it is unconscionable.

title: Distress for Rent
bodyText: West Virginia still allows distress for rent, but only through the courts: rent may be distrained for within one year after it falls due, whether or not the lease has ended, by the sheriff or a deputy sheriff under a warrant a magistrate issues on your affidavit that the rent is justly due. The levy may reach goods of the tenant, an assignee or a subtenant found on the premises or removed within the past 30 days, subject to liens that already existed when the goods were brought onto the premises and to perfected purchase-money security interests. If the tenant intends to remove, is removing, or has within the past 30 days removed belongings from the premises, and you swear that without an attachment there will not be enough property left on the premises to cover the rent, a magistrate may issue an order of attachment for rent that will become payable within one year, after you post the bond the statute requires. A tenant whose property is distrained for rent not due, or attached without good cause, can sue for damages. A resident tenant may set apart property exempt from execution or other process (for example up to $8,000 in household goods), which likely includes distress, and a waiver of those exemptions is void. Never seize a tenant's belongings yourself.

title: Rental Inspections
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets up a state rental inspection program or requires an inspection before renting. Counties and cities may adopt building and housing codes, and may adopt ordinances to repair, close, vacate or demolish unsafe or unsanitary dwellings. A statute in the Municipal Home Rule Program section also says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals, and may regulate activities that arise from rental use only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not. Whether that reaches every city, and whether it rules out a registration or inspection ordinance that applies only to rentals, is unsettled. A city code enforcement official must give the owner reasonable advance notice and ask permission to enter (except in exigent circumstances); if the owner cannot be found or refuses, the official may get an administrative search warrant and must give the owner, and any tenant in possession, a copy five days before entering. You must keep a rental in compliance with applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes unless a violation is the fault of the tenant, the tenant's family or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent.

title: Unfit or Condemned Units
bodyText: No West Virginia statute bars collecting rent for a unit that has been condemned or declared unfit for human habitation, or requires you to relocate the tenant. The tenant's protection comes from your duty to keep the unit fit and habitable and in compliance with health, safety, fire and housing codes, and from the casualty rule: if the building is destroyed in whole or part by fire or otherwise without the tenant's fault or negligence, rent is reasonably reduced for buildings the tenant does not own and cannot remove (unless the lease provides otherwise) and the tenant may surrender possession if you do not rebuild as soon as you reasonably can. Cities and counties may adopt ordinances to vacate and close or demolish unsafe dwellings, and a city may charge the owner its costs and file a lien. The habitability statute does not require repairs while the tenant is behind on rent, but only where the lease promises no more: a greater repair duty in the lease controls, and the Landlord Maintenance clause this library uses for West Virginia promises repairs without an exception for unpaid rent.

title: Association Rules and Rentals
bodyText:
If the unit is in a condominium, cooperative or planned community under West Virginia's Uniform Common Interest Ownership Act, the declaration, bylaws and association rules govern leasing, and no provision found sets a fee for leasing a unit or lets the association collect rent from your tenant. An amendment changing the uses to which a unit is restricted needs the unanimous consent of the unit owners unless the Act expressly permits otherwise; whether a new leasing restriction is such a change is not settled by the text.

The association may levy reasonable fines for violations of the declaration, bylaws and rules after notice and an opportunity to be heard; the Act does not say whether it may fine a tenant directly. The declaration may give lessees the vote on specified matters. For a community created before the Act took effect, generally only listed parts of the Act apply, and the unanimous-consent rule is not among them; but an older community may amend its declaration under the Act, and an older condominium is also governed by the earlier condominium law, so check how its declaration may be amended.

Read the declaration, bylaws and rules before leasing a unit.

title: Medical Cannabis in Rentals
bodyText: West Virginia allows only medical cannabis, for certified patients and caregivers with a valid identification card, and only in forms such as pills, oils, topicals, tinctures, liquids, dermal patches and forms for vaporization or nebulization. Smoking medical cannabis is unlawful, and so is growing it without a permit; other marijuana possession remains a crime. The Medical Cannabis Act protects patients from arrest, prosecution or penalty, or denial of any right or privilege, solely for lawful use, but says nothing about rental housing. A lease may prohibit smoking and growing; whether you may bar a patient's lawful non-smoked use, or refuse to rent to a patient, is not settled by the text.

title: Renting an Accessory Dwelling Unit
bodyText: Under a West Virginia law in effect since June 4, 2026, a city or town may not adopt a policy, regulation or ordinance that restricts, prohibits or otherwise regulates the use of at least one accessory dwelling unit by right on a lot with a single-family dwelling. An accessory dwelling unit is a self-contained, independently accessed living unit with its own cooking, sleeping and sanitation facilities on the same parcel as a larger single-family dwelling; it may be attached, detached or internal, and an attached or detached unit may be no larger than 75 percent of the main dwelling's floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is less, and a manufactured home on a permanent foundation may be one. The municipality may not require a family, marital or employment relationship between the occupants of the main dwelling and of the accessory unit, so you may rent it to an unrelated tenant, and it may not require extra parking, separate water and sewer, or a restrictive covenant. It may charge no more than $250 to review an application (plus its usual building fees) and no more than $250 in development impact fees, and may require will-serve letters from the water and sewer systems. A conflicting local rule in effect on or after January 1, 2027 is invalid to the extent of the conflict. The law does not stop a municipality from regulating short-term rentals of 30 days or less, does not override building, fire and other regulatory requirements, and does not bar private restrictive covenants such as association rules; it speaks only of municipalities, not counties.

title: Penalty for Mishandling a Deposit
bodyText: If you fail to follow West Virginia's security deposit law and the failure is willful or not in good faith, the tenant can get a judgment for any deposit you did not return plus damages for annoyance or inconvenience equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld. If the tenant owes you rent, the court credits that award against the rent due. A lease term in which the tenant gives up any deposit right is unenforceable, and if you sue to enforce one, the tenant can recover actual damages and reasonable attorney's fees. Deposit cases are heard in magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the rental is located, and the tenant's other remedies are not limited.

title: Holding a Deposit and Keeping Records
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute requires a landlord who holds tenants' deposits personally to keep them in a separate or escrow account, at any particular bank, or to pay interest on them. A licensed real estate broker (including a broker acting as your property manager) who holds deposits for you rather than passing them to you at once must keep them in a federally insured trust fund account, not mixed with the broker's own money, that does not earn interest unless a Real Estate Commission rule allows it.

You must keep itemized records of every deduction you make from a tenant's deposit because the tenant did not comply with the lease, for one year after the tenancy ends. Within 72 hours after a written request, during normal business hours, you must either let the tenant (or the tenant's authorized agent or attorney) inspect that tenant's record of deductions or, at your option, give them a copy.

title: No Interest on Deposits
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to pay interest on a security deposit.

title: No Limit on Deposit Amount
bodyText: West Virginia does not limit how much you can charge as a security deposit. A refundable pet deposit, and a pet fee or application fee that the tenant has not expressly agreed in writing is nonrefundable, is part of the security deposit and is returned under the deposit rules. Prepaid rent is not a security deposit. You may not charge any deposit or fee for an assistance animal.

title: Deposits When the Property Is Sold
bodyText: Whoever holds the landlord's interest in the property when a tenancy ends is bound by West Virginia's deposit rules and must return any deposit the original landlord received that is owed to the tenant. That is true however the interest was acquired or transferred, whether or not the deposit was handed over, and whatever the seller and buyer agreed between themselves. A buyer should therefore account for tenants' deposits at closing. If a tenant has an assignee or subtenant, you may hold a deposit from only one of them.

title: Pet Deposits, Pet Fees and Pet Rent
bodyText: West Virginia does not cap pet deposits, pet fees or pet rent. A refundable pet deposit is a security deposit, held and returned under the deposit rules. A pet fee is outside those rules only if you and the tenant expressly agree in writing that it is nonrefundable; use the lease's Nonrefundable Fees terms to do that. Monthly pet rent is rent (this library's reading). You may not charge a pet fee, deposit or other pet charge for an assistance animal a tenant needs because of a disability.

title: Application Fees
bodyText: West Virginia does not cap rental application fees or require a refund when an applicant is turned down. An application fee is outside the security deposit rules only if you and the applicant expressly agree in writing that it is nonrefundable, so put that statement in the signed application.

title: Last Month's Rent and the Deposit
bodyText: Prepaid rent, such as last month's rent collected at signing, is not a security deposit in West Virginia. A tenant cannot require you to treat the security deposit as payment of the last month's rent: the deposit statute says that nothing in it entitles a tenant, when the tenancy ends, to an immediate credit of the deposit against unpaid rent. You apply the deposit after the tenancy ends, within the return period, to rent due and the other permitted charges.

title: Move-In Condition Records
bodyText: West Virginia does not require a move-in inspection, condition checklist or signed inventory. Because deductions for damage are reduced by reasonable wear and tear, a dated written record of the property's condition at move-in, with photos signed or acknowledged by the tenant, is the practical way to support deductions later.

title: Tenant Utility Bills and Liens on Your Property
bodyText:
Whether a tenant's unpaid water, sewer or stormwater bill can be charged to you or become a lien on your rental depends on which West Virginia statute the utility operates under. For a city waterworks, a city sewer service where another provider supplies the water, a combined city water and sewer system, and a public service district, the statute says an owner may not be held liable for a tenant's delinquent charges, and no lien attaches to the property for them, unless the owner contracted directly with the utility for the service.

Other statutes, for city sewerage and stormwater works, other city public works (only if the city's ordinance so provides), and the general section on water shutoffs for unpaid sewer and stormwater bills, which covers privately owned and homeowners' association utilities among others, make unpaid charges a lien on the premises served with no exception for a tenant's bill; city sewerage charges are payable by the property owner, and city stormwater charges by the owner or any user. Before relying on a tenant's own account, ask the utility which law it bills under and whether a tenant's unpaid bill can become a lien.

A city may not have a lien for unpaid garbage collection fees, but may adopt an ordinance allowing liens for unpaid fire, police or street fees after at least 90 days' certified-mail notice to the owner.

title: Squatters and Unauthorized Occupants
bodyText: Since July 10, 2025, West Virginia's Stop Squatters Act lets a property owner or authorized agent ask a law enforcement officer to remove a squatter from a residential dwelling without going to court, by submitting a completed and verified complaint, if: the person is unlawfully occupying the property; the property was not open to the public when the person entered; you told the person to leave; the person is not a current or former owner or lawful tenant, or an immediate family member of the owner or tenants; and no litigation about the property is pending between you and the person. After preliminary fact-finding, the agency serves a notice to vacate immediately, puts you in possession, and on request removes a person who does not leave; it may charge a fee for serving the notice. The Act defines a squatter as someone unlawfully occupying who is not entitled under a rental or lease agreement or is not authorized by the tenant or owner to be there, and police removal is only for an unauthorized person who is not a current or former lawful tenant, so it does not reach a guest the tenant let in or a current or former tenant, including one holding over; for them, use the court eviction process. A bad-faith complaint can be prosecuted as false swearing, and a person wrongly removed can sue for possession, costs, damages and attorney fees. Separately, knowingly listing or advertising residential property for rent without legal title or authority is a felony, so check the authority of anyone who offers to rent property to you or to manage it for you, and watch for copies of your own listings posted by someone else.

title: Guests' Rights
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute gives tenants or their guests rights that limit a lease's guest terms, apart from fair housing law. Under the Stop Squatters Act, police removal is only for an unauthorized person unlawfully occupying the property, and not for a member of the tenant's immediate family, so a guest the tenant has authorized, or a member of the tenant's immediate family, cannot be removed under that process; whether a former guest whose permission has ended can be is not settled. A guest problem is handled under the lease and, if necessary, the court eviction process against the tenant.

The one statutory guest right is for a factory-built (manufactured) home rental community: there, a tenant's invitee has free access to the tenant's home site without charge unless a court has ordered otherwise.

title: Children and Familial Status
bodyText: West Virginia's Fair Housing Act bars refusing to rent to, or setting different terms for, a household because of familial status: a child under 18 living with a parent, a legal custodian or their designee with written permission, or a person who is pregnant or securing legal custody of a child. You also may not advertise a preference against children. Reasonable local, state or federal limits on the maximum number of occupants still apply, and qualifying housing for older persons is exempt from the familial-status rules. A rooming house occupied by the owner, with no more than four rooms rented or for rent, is exempt from most of the Act's rental prohibitions, familial status included. For familial status only, the Act also exempts a single-family house rented by a private owner of no more than three such houses, without a broker or a discriminatory advertisement, and rooms or units in a building for up to four families where the owner lives in one of them.

title: Registered Sex Offenders as Tenants
bodyText: West Virginia's residence limits for sex offenders apply only to certain people on court-ordered extended supervised release of 10 years to life: they may not establish a residence within 1,000 feet of a school, a child care facility or a victim's residence, and one convicted of a sexually violent offense against a child may not live in a household where a child under 16 lives unless the person is the child's parent, grandparent or a qualifying stepparent; a court may also impose other residency conditions. These limits bind the supervised person, not the landlord. No West Virginia statute requires a landlord to screen applicants against the registry, disclose a registrant to other tenants, or refuse to rent to one; registrants must report the address of their residence and of any home they lease and regularly visit.

title: Building Rules and Regulations
bodyText: No West Virginia statute governs rules and regulations for ordinary residential rentals, so a rule binds a tenant as a term of the lease: attach the rules to the lease or have the tenant sign for them. Whether you can add or change rules during the term depends on what the lease says and on contract law. A written residential rental agreement, including rules made part of it, must be clear and coherent, use words with common and everyday meanings, be printed in easily readable type and be organized and captioned so it is easily understood; a violation does not void the agreement, but a tenant whose request to conform it is refused may sue to have it reformed. West Virginia's statutory test for enforceable rules applies only to factory-built (manufactured) home rental communities.

title: Firearms
bodyText: West Virginia's Constitution protects the right to keep and bear arms for the defense of self, family, home and state. No West Virginia statute addresses a private landlord's lease rules on firearms inside a rented home. An owner, lessee or other person in charge of real property may prohibit carrying firearms on property under their control, and a person who refuses a request to give up the firearm temporarily or to leave commits a misdemeanor; whether that lets you bar firearms inside a unit leased to and controlled by the tenant is not settled. The same law bars an owner or lessee from prohibiting a customer, employee or invitee from keeping a lawfully possessed firearm out of view and locked in or to a vehicle in a parking lot, or from searching the vehicle for one; whether a residential tenant counts as a customer or invitee is not settled, so the safer course is not to ban guns kept locked and out of view in vehicles. Firing a gun within 500 feet of a dwelling house is generally a misdemeanor, with a narrow exception for residents. Cities may not limit firearm possession in a way that conflicts with state law.

title: Smoking, Vaping and Medical Cannabis
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute regulates smoking or vaping in private rental housing or limits a lease's no-smoking terms, so the lease governs; local board of health rules and ordinances may add limits. West Virginia's cannabis law is a medical program: use of medical cannabis is lawful only as that act allows, and the act makes it unlawful to smoke medical cannabis. Medical cannabis may be dispensed as pills, oils, topical forms, tinctures, liquids, dermal patches and forms for vaporization or nebulization, but not in dry leaf or plant form unless the state bureau's rules allow it.

The act says a patient or caregiver may not be denied any right or privilege solely for lawful use, but it says nothing about leases or landlords, so whether a lease may bar lawful medical use other than smoking, such as vaping, is unsettled; a ban on smoking cannabis matches state law.

title: Tenant Duties Set by Statute
bodyText:
West Virginia has no general statute listing a residential tenant's duties; most come from the lease. A few statutes reach tenants. A tenant who commits waste on the property while in possession, without the owner's special permission, is liable for the damage. In a one- or two-family dwelling the owner does not live in, the tenant must do routine maintenance on the smoke detectors. Your duties to meet housing codes and make repairs do not cover conditions caused by the fault of, or repairs needed primarily because of a lack of reasonable care by, the tenant, a family member or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent.

A lease promise to leave the premises in good repair means returning them in good and substantial repair, reasonable wear and tear excepted, and does not oblige the tenant to rebuild after a fire or other destruction that was not the tenant's fault unless other words show that intent. Deliberately or negligently damaging the property, or knowingly letting someone else do so, is a ground for a summary eviction case.

title: Renter's Insurance Requirements
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates whether or how a landlord may require a tenant to carry renter's insurance, so a lease's insurance requirement is a contract term.

title: Tenant Security Cameras
bodyText: No West Virginia statute addresses tenant-installed security cameras or video doorbells, so the lease's alterations terms govern installation. The only statute on surveillance cameras on private land limits law enforcement officers, not landlords or tenants.

title: Flags, Signs and Other Displays
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives tenants a right to display a flag, a political sign or a religious or cultural item despite a lease restriction, so the lease's display terms govern. Apply them evenly: fair housing law bars different terms because of religion or national origin.

title: Portable Solar Devices
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives tenants a right to install a portable or plug-in solar device. The state's solar access law voids only restrictions in a housing association's governing documents executed or recorded after it took effect, and only for solar energy systems affixed to a building; it does not govern leases.

title: Waterbeds
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates waterbeds or other liquid-filled furniture in rentals, so the lease's terms govern.

title: Tenant Absences
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a tenant to tell you about an extended absence, or gives you a right to enter during one, so any notice requirement is a lease term. If a tenant who owes rent abandons the property, you may post a written notice on the property requiring payment within one month; if the rent is not paid by then, you are entitled to possession and may enter.

title: How Rent May Be Paid
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to accept cash or any particular payment method, or bars requiring rent to be paid electronically, so the lease's payment terms govern.

title: Landlord Entry
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute sets a notice period, hours or permitted purposes for a landlord's entry into a residential rental, so the lease's access terms govern, subject to the tenant's right to possession under case law; state in the lease how much notice you will give and when you may enter without notice. Statutes address entry only in narrow cases. If a tenant who owes rent abandons the property and does not pay within one month after you post a written notice, you are entitled to possession and may enter.

A cable operator asked to provide service may enter a building of three or more households to survey or install after serving notice on you and the tenant. If a tenant refuses entry that the lease allows, the refusal breaches a lease covenant, which is a ground for a summary eviction case, so document your request and the refusal.

title: Cable and Broadband Access
bodyText: If you own or manage premises with dwelling units for three or more households, including a mobile home park, West Virginia bars you from interfering with the installation, maintenance, operation or removal of cable television facilities, from taking any payment from a tenant for permitting cable service, from taking payment from a cable operator beyond just compensation set under the law, and from charging different rent to tenants who do and do not receive cable. You may require that installation meet reasonable conditions to protect the safety, functioning and appearance of the premises and other tenants' convenience, that the cable operator or tenant bear the full cost of installation or removal, and that the operator indemnify you for damage. The operator must give you written notice at least 15 days before installing; the tenant must get the same written notice, or verbal notice of the date and time of entry at least 24 hours ahead. You are entitled to a single payment of just compensation, set by the Public Service Commission if you cannot agree, but not for a later rebuild, upgrade or rewiring. Separately, an agreement or contract made effective after West Virginia's broadband law took effect may not regulate or prevent exterior installation of antennas and equipment used for broadband; whether that reaches a residential lease is unsettled.

title: Fire Sprinklers
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to install or retrofit fire sprinklers in an existing rental. Sprinkler requirements come from the State Fire Code, which has the force of law statewide, and the State Building Code in counties and cities that adopt it. The State Fire Code requires automatic sprinklers in new buildings it covers (it does not cover buildings used wholly as dwellings for no more than two families), and its own text adds no retrofit duty for existing rentals. For the posted sprinkler sign, see Sprinkler and Window Signs. In a one- or two-family dwelling, an automatic fire sprinkler system installed under the State Fire Code and State Building Code may be provided instead of the required smoke detectors.

title: Water Heater Temperature
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets a water heater temperature or requires a landlord to set or check it. If the dwelling unit is supplied by direct public utility connections, you must supply reasonable amounts of hot water at all times, unless the hot water comes from an installation within the tenant's exclusive control.

title: Liens for Work a Tenant Orders
bodyText: West Virginia's mechanics' lien law gives a contractor, supplier or worker a lien on a building and on the owner's interest in the land when the work is done under a contract with the owner. No West Virginia statute says whether improvements a tenant orders can bind the landlord's interest, or lets a lease or a recorded notice protect the landlord. Whether a contractor hired by a tenant can reach your interest, for example where you approved the work, depends on case law. Requiring your written consent before alterations, and requiring the tenant to pay for any work the tenant orders, are lease terms between you and the tenant.

title: Domestic Violence and the Tenancy
bodyText: West Virginia has no statute giving a tenant rights because of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, such as a right to end the lease early, to have the locks changed or to avoid eviction, so there is no statutory list of documents a tenant must give you. Court orders can still affect a tenancy: a family court protective order may grant the victim possession of the residence the parties shared and order the abuser to stay away from the victim's residence, though it cannot affect title to real property, and a magistrate's personal safety order may order a person not to enter the petitioner's residence. Follow any such order you are shown.

title: Home-Based Businesses
bodyText:
West Virginia makes using a residential dwelling for a home-based business a permitted use. A home-based business is one owned and operated by the owner or tenant of the dwelling and carried on inside it, limited to the sale of lawful goods and services, that does not generate on-street parking or a substantial increase in traffic and has no signage visible from the street. A city may adopt reasonable regulations and may limit or prohibit some activities, such as selling illegal drugs or products containing alcohol or tobacco, operating a sober living home or operating a vape shop, but may not require rezoning, fire sprinklers in a dwelling of one or two units, or a license not required of similar businesses.

The permission does not override any deed restriction, covenant or agreement restricting the use of land, or a common interest community's documents, so a lease limiting the property to residential use still binds the tenant; if you will allow a home business, say so in the lease and set your conditions.

title: Returned Check Fees and Remedies
bodyText:
If a tenant's check is dishonored for insufficient funds or credit, West Virginia lets you, as the payee, charge a fee of up to $25. You may not impose or collect the fee after a complaint for a worthless-check warrant has been delivered to magistrate court, and once a complaint has been presented there, payment may be made only through the court. State the fee in the lease and keep it at $25 or less. No statute authorizes a fee for a failed electronic payment, so this library's Returned Payments clause charges none, though it lets you require certified funds to replace any failed payment.

If the tenant knowingly fails to pay the check amount in cash within 30 days after your written demand, you may sue for the face amount, damages of $500 or the face amount (whichever is less) and reasonable filing costs, but you may not use both that civil remedy and the criminal worthless-check procedure for the same check. The criminal worthless-check statutes do not apply to a postdated check, or to a check you knew or had reason to believe was not covered when you accepted it.

title: No Statutory Grace Period
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives residential tenants a grace period before rent is late or before a late fee may be charged, so any grace period is up to the lease. Rent is due on the date the lease sets. You may take a late charge out of the security deposit only if it is reasonable and specified in the rental agreement, so state the due date, any grace period and the late fee in the lease.

title: Rent Increase Notice
bodyText:
Apart from the temporary limit on month-to-month rent during a declared state of emergency or preparedness (see the disaster row), no West Virginia statute sets a notice period, frequency limit or cap for raising rent on a home. During a fixed-term lease, the rent stays as the lease states unless the lease provides for an increase; this library's optional Mid-Term Rent Increase clause requires 30 days' written notice and lets the tenant end the lease without a fee instead.

For a periodic tenancy, give written notice of the new rent at least as far ahead as the notice needed to end the tenancy: a full rental period before the end of a period for month-to-month or week-to-week, and three months before the end of a year for year-to-year, unless your lease fixes a different notice period. Avoid raising rent soon after a tenant's complaint; see the retaliation row for how retaliation can be raised.

title: Raising Rent During a Lease Term
bodyText: No West Virginia statute addresses a lease term that lets you raise rent during a fixed term, and none forbids one. Without such a term, the rent stated in a fixed-term lease applies for the whole term. If you want the right to raise rent mid-lease, the lease must say so, including when an increase can take effect, how much notice you will give and how the new rent is set. This library offers an optional Mid-Term Rent Increase clause: you give at least 30 days' written notice of the new rent, and the tenant may instead end the lease without a fee before the increase takes effect.

title: Rent Control and Local Rent Limits
bodyText: Apart from the emergency limit below, no West Virginia statute caps the rent a private landlord may charge or how much it may be raised, and no statute expressly allows or forbids local rent control. A provision of the municipal home rule law says municipalities may not prohibit or effectively limit the rental of a property, or regulate the duration, frequency or location of rentals. A municipality may regulate activities that arise when a property is used as a rental only if the regulation applies uniformly to all properties, rented or not (local hotel occupancy taxes are allowed). Whether these limits would bar a local limit on rent amounts is for the courts. Check your city's ordinances. During a declared state of emergency or state of preparedness a temporary price limit applies to month-to-month rentals (see the disaster row).

title: Algorithmic Rent Pricing
bodyText: No West Virginia statute specifically regulates using software or an algorithm to set rent. West Virginia's antitrust act does apply to renting homes: it makes unlawful any contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade, including an agreement between two or more persons for the purpose or with the effect of fixing, controlling or maintaining a market price, rate or fee. Anyone injured in their business or property may sue for three times their damages plus attorney's fees and costs. Set your rents independently and don't share nonpublic rent data with competitors; federal antitrust law also applies.

title: Are Fees Rent?
bodyText:
In West Virginia's security deposit law, rent means all money owed or paid to you under the rental agreement other than a security deposit, a nonrefundable fee or a payment for damage the tenant caused. Reasonable late charges specified in the lease are applied with rent when you apply the deposit at move-out. Recurring charges the lease calls rent, such as pet rent, should count as rent too, but the statute does not say so expressly, and in any case you may apply the deposit to other charges the lease provides for. That definition applies only within the deposit law.

The eviction statute lets you seek possession when a tenant is in arrears in the payment of rent but does not define rent, and no statute settles whether an unpaid fee alone is unpaid rent. This library's lease does not make an unpaid late fee, by itself, grounds for ending the lease.

title: Collection Fees and Notice Fees
bodyText: Don't charge a tenant a collection-agency fee, or a fee for preparing or serving a notice, unless a statute authorizes it. West Virginia's consumer debt-collection law, which by its words reaches anyone collecting a debt that arose from a transaction for personal, family or household purposes, bars collecting any part of a debt collector's fee for its services, collecting a fee incidental to the debt unless both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it, and saying that a debt can be increased by fees that cannot legally be added. A violation can cost actual damages plus a $1,000 penalty for each violation. No West Virginia statute authorizes a residential landlord to charge collection costs or notice fees, so this library's lease includes neither.

title: Fees Must Be in the Lease
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential lease to list every fee or sets a notice period for adding one; the rule that a landlord may not collect a fee not listed in the rental agreement applies only to factory-built home sites. Several West Virginia rules still turn on the lease's words: you may apply the deposit to late charges only if they are specified in the rental agreement, and to other charges only as the rental agreement provides; a pet or application fee is outside the deposit only if the tenant expressly agrees in writing that it is nonrefundable; and, if the consumer debt-collection law applies, a fee added because of a default or for collection, such as a late fee, returned-check fee or collection cost, can be collected only if both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it. Rent, reimbursement of an actual cost the lease makes the tenant's, and the price of an option the tenant chooses, such as an early-termination fee, are part of what the tenant agreed to pay. List every fee in the lease and add one mid-term only with the tenant's written agreement. You may not charge any fee or deposit for an assistance animal.

title: No Rent Receipt Requirement
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires a residential landlord to give a receipt for each rent payment, even rent paid in cash. One narrow exception: if a tenant aged 65 or older, with household income of no more than $5,000, claims West Virginia's senior citizens' homestead tax relief and asks, you must sign a statement of the gross rent the tenant paid for the year; willfully failing to do so, or willfully giving a false or fraudulent statement, is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $50. The state's consumer-credit receipt rule covers consumer credit sales, consumer loans and consumer leases of goods, not leases of homes. Giving a written receipt for every cash payment and keeping a rent ledger is still good practice, and helps if the amount owed is disputed in court.

title: Rent Concessions
bodyText: No West Virginia statute regulates rent concessions or move-in specials. If you offer one, state it clearly in the lease, including whether and when you may recover it if the tenant leaves early or defaults.

title: No Government Shutdown Protection
bodyText: No West Virginia statute protects tenants who are federal or state employees from eviction, late fees or other remedies during a government shutdown. The lease and the usual eviction rules apply.

title: Interest on Unpaid Rent and Damages
bodyText: In an action for rent, West Virginia allows interest as on other contracts. The court may award prejudgment interest on special or liquidated damages; if the obligation is based on a written agreement, it bears interest until judgment at the rate the agreement sets, and otherwise at a statutory rate of two percentage points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year the claim arose, but not less than 4% or more than 9% a year. A judgment then bears simple interest at the rate figured the same way for the year it is entered. The general legal rate of interest is 6% a year. This library's lease sets no contract interest rate.

title: Unclaimed Security Deposits
bodyText:
West Virginia's unclaimed property law lists a security deposit as property a holder must turn over to the State Treasurer when the owner doesn't claim it. If you hold deposits in the course of your rental business, a refund you owe a former tenant is presumed abandoned three years after the tenant became entitled to it if the tenant has not contacted you about it in that time.

You must then report it and pay it to the Treasurer: reports are due before November 1 each year, covering the 12 months before July 1, and for $50 or more you must first send the tenant written notice 60 to 120 days before filing if you have an address not known to be wrong and the tenant's claim is not time-barred. The deposit law does not let you keep a refund the tenant does not collect; if personal delivery is not reasonably possible and a mailed refund comes back undeliverable, hold it six months for the tenant to claim, then keep it for the unclaimed property process.

Late reports carry 12% interest and daily civil penalties; paying the Treasurer in good faith ends your liability for the money.

title: Holding Deposits
bodyText: No West Virginia statute specifically regulates a holding deposit taken before a lease is signed. The deposit law treats money, however labeled, paid to be considered as a tenant as an application fee, and any refundable money given to secure performance of a rental agreement as a security deposit; prepaid rent is neither. Unless you and the applicant expressly agree in writing that a payment is a nonrefundable application fee, treat a holding deposit as a refundable security deposit, applied and returned under the deposit rules. Put in writing what the payment is for, whether it will be credited to the deposit or first month's rent, and when and how it will be refunded if no lease is signed.

title: Paying a Deposit in Installments
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives a tenant the right to pay a security deposit in installments or requires you to offer that option. If you agree to installments, put the schedule in writing; every installment is part of the security deposit and is held and returned under the deposit rules.

title: Fees Instead of a Deposit
bodyText: No West Virginia statute authorizes or regulates a fee or insurance product offered in place of a security deposit. Under the deposit law, any refundable money a tenant gives to secure performance or cover damage is a security deposit, while a nonrefundable fee is neither a deposit nor rent, so a genuinely nonrefundable fee in lieu of a deposit falls outside the deposit rules. If you offer one, say in writing that it is nonrefundable and whether it limits the tenant's liability for damage. Deposit insurance and surety products are governed by insurance law. This library offers no fee-in-lieu clause.

title: Preset Cleaning and Damage Charges
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets or forbids a lease schedule of preset cleaning, carpet or repair charges. When the tenancy ends you may apply the deposit to damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the lease, less reasonable wear and tear, and to other damages or charges the rental agreement provides for, with a written itemization. A preset charge the tenant pays whatever the unit's condition, such as repainting or carpet cleaning after normal use, risks being treated as a charge for reasonable wear and tear or as a waiver of the tenant's deposit rights; the statute does not settle it. If you use a schedule, tie each charge to actual damage or uncleanliness beyond normal wear and itemize it.

title: What Counts as an Assistance Animal
bodyText:
Under West Virginia's Fair Housing Act, an assistance animal is any service, therapy or support animal weighing less than 150 pounds, with or without specific training or certification, that works, provides assistance or performs tasks for a person with a disability, or provides emotional support that alleviates one or more identified symptoms or effects of the disability. A request for one is a request for a reasonable accommodation to your animal rules: it may not be unreasonably denied or delayed, or conditioned on a fee, deposit or other terms that apply to pets.

These rules reach small landlords too; the exemptions are narrow (see the fair housing row). An animal of 150 pounds or more is outside the state definition, but the general duty to make reasonable accommodations, and federal law, may still require you to consider the request.

title: Misrepresenting a Service Animal
bodyText: In West Virginia it is a misdemeanor to falsely claim that an animal is a service animal, or that you are blind or have a disability, to obtain the rights the state's White Cane law gives in public places, public transportation, hotels, lodging places and other places of public accommodation. The penalty is a fine of up to $200, up to 10 days in jail, or both, rising to $1,000, 30 days, or both for a repeat offense. That law does not by its terms reach a request to keep an assistance animal in a rental home, and no West Virginia statute penalizes a false assistance-animal request in housing. Handle housing requests under the fair housing rules, which let you ask for documentation from a professional treatment provider of the disability-related need.

title: Towing and Abandoned Vehicles
bodyText:
West Virginia requires no towing signs at a private lot, but a vehicle parked on private property without the permission of the owner, tenant or lessee may be moved at the vehicle owner's cost; whoever removes it must notify the State Police and, inside a city or town, the municipal police, and the tow must be done by a wrecker company authorized by the Public Service Commission (see Parking Rules and Towing From Your Lot). A vehicle left on private property without the consent of the owner or person in control for more than five days is an abandoned motor vehicle, and abandoning one there is a misdemeanor.

Police and other enforcement agencies may take it, but only after sending you and the vehicle's owner, if known, 30 days' notice by registered or certified mail; the owner and lienholders may then reclaim it within 10 days of notice by paying the towing and storage charges. Tow companies' maximum rates for wrecked or disabled vehicles are set by the Public Service Commission. A tenant's vehicle parked with your permission is not abandoned; enforce parking rules through the lease, and check local ordinances before towing.

title: No Tenant Right to EV Charging
bodyText: No West Virginia statute gives tenants a right to install an electric vehicle charger or requires landlords to provide charging. A tenant who wants a charger needs your consent under the lease's alterations terms; if you agree, put the installation, electricity cost, insurance and removal at move-out in writing.

title: Storage Units and the Self-Storage Lien Act
bodyText: West Virginia's Self-Service Storage Lien Act gives operators of self-service storage facilities a lien on stored property and a sale procedure, but it works through a storage rental agreement that must contain the statements the Act requires. Unlike the state's storage-insurance statute, the lien Act does not expressly exclude storage rented with a home, so whether it reaches a storage unit you rent to a tenant with an apartment is not settled by statute. This library's storage clause does not invoke the Act. Treat belongings a tenant leaves in a storage space like other property left behind at the end of a tenancy.

title: Out-of-State Landlords
bodyText: No West Virginia statute requires an out-of-state individual landlord to appoint an agent in West Virginia. An out-of-state entity is different. A foreign limited liability company that owns income-producing real property in West Virginia is transacting business here, so it needs a certificate of authority from the Secretary of State. Until it has one, it may not maintain an eviction or any other action or proceeding in West Virginia. Its leases stay valid, and while it is unregistered it is treated as having appointed the Secretary of State as its agent for service of process on claims arising from its business here (W. Va. Code §§ 31B-10-1003(b), 31B-10-1008). A foreign limited partnership transacting business here may not bring a suit in any court until it registers, though its leases stay valid and it may defend a suit; by doing business without registering it appoints the Secretary of State to accept service in cases arising from that business (W. Va. Code § 47-9-54). A foreign corporation needs a certificate of authority to conduct affairs here. If it transacts business without one, it may not maintain a proceeding in a circuit court until it gets one, and it owes the fees and taxes it would have paid. Owning real property, without more, is not conducting affairs, so whether renting it out is depends on the facts; get advice before filing. An unregistered corporation doing business here is presumed to have appointed the Secretary of State to accept service for it (W. Va. Code §§ 31D-15-1501, 31D-15-1502, 31D-15-1510(e)). If you rent under a name other than your own, or other than your entity's registered name, you must first file the name with the Secretary of State. Willfully failing to is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $25 to $100, up to 30 days in jail, or both (W. Va. Code §§ 47-8-2, 47-8-4, 47-8-5). Separately, a nonresident who has an interest in, uses or possesses real property in West Virginia is treated as having appointed the Secretary of State to receive process in a circuit court case arising from it; the Secretary of State mails the papers to your out-of-state address by registered or certified mail, and a default judgment may be entered if you don't appear and defend within 30 days. Keep your address current and consider naming a local manager to receive notices. Under the deposit law, a managing agent who does not disclose the owner's name is treated as the landlord.

title: Changing Terms of a Periodic Tenancy
bodyText: No West Virginia statute sets a notice period for changing the terms or rules of a periodic tenancy, such as a month-to-month lease. A change the tenant has not agreed to is safest with written notice at least as far ahead as the notice needed to end the tenancy (a full rental period before the end of a period for month-to-month or week-to-week, three months before the end of a year for year-to-year), so the tenant can choose to leave. During a fixed term, change terms only as the lease allows or with the tenant's written agreement.

title: Accepting Rent After a Default
bodyText: No West Virginia statute says whether accepting rent, or part of the rent, after a tenant's default or after a notice to quit waives your right to end a residential tenancy or seek possession. That is a question of case law. If you accept a payment after giving notice or filing for possession, say in writing that you accept it without waiving the default or your right to possession. Separately, in an ejectment or unlawful detainer case for unpaid rent, a statute ends the case if all the rent and arrears, with interest and costs, are paid or tendered to you or your attorney, or paid into court, before trial (see the redemption row).

title: Taxes on Rent
bodyText: Counties and cities may impose a hotel occupancy tax on hotel rooms, which include boarding houses, condominiums, cabins, lodges and tourist homes where the public can rent sleeping accommodations. The tax does not apply to sleeping accommodations rented month-to-month or for 30 days or longer from the start at a boarding house, condominium, cabin, tourist home, apartment or home. Where it applies, the operator collects it from the guest, states it separately on bills and may not advertise that it will absorb it; if you rent through a booking platform that meets the statute's sales thresholds, the platform must collect and remit it for you. No West Virginia statute expressly taxes ordinary long-term residential rent. If you rent short-term, ask your county or city and the State Tax Department whether occupancy tax or consumers sales tax applies.

title: Late Fees
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute caps a late fee on a residential lease or sets a grace period before one may be charged. State the fee and when it applies in the lease and keep it reasonable: you may take late charges out of the security deposit only if they are reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement. West Virginia's consumer debt-collection law bars collecting a charge incidental to an obligation unless both the agreement and a statute or regulation expressly authorize it, with a penalty of up to $1,000 per violation; it does not say whether it reaches rent, and this library reads the deposit statute's recognition of reasonable, agreed late charges as that authority.

A very large fee also risks being treated as an unenforceable penalty. Unpaid rent separately bears interest as on other contracts. This library's lease does not let you end the tenancy for an unpaid late fee alone.

title: Land Taken by Eminent Domain
bodyText: If all of the leased property is taken by eminent domain (condemnation for public use), the tenant's duty to pay rent ends, unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. If only part of the property, or an easement or other interest in it, is taken, the rent is reduced in proportion to the value of what was taken compared with the whole, again unless the lease expressly provides otherwise. These rules don't affect any right the tenant has to compensation from the condemning authority for the value of the lease or the tenant's property, beyond the rent the tenant no longer owes. This library's lease leaves these rules in place.

title: Municipal Service Fees
bodyText: West Virginia cities may charge reasonable fees for services such as police and fire protection, street maintenance and lighting, and garbage collection, imposed by ordinance on the users of the service; in a rental, the tenant may be the user billed. A city may not have a lien on property for these fees, except that it may adopt an ordinance allowing a lien on real property for unpaid fire, police or street fees after at least 90 days' notice to the owner by certified mail. A lease may lawfully require the tenant to reimburse you for a fee billed to you, but this library does not offer such a clause: who is billed varies by city and ordinance, and the tenant is often billed directly as the user. If you want one, add your own clause after taking advice, and state the fee, its amount and how you will bill it in the lease.

title: Habitability Rules West Virginia Does Not Have
bodyText: West Virginia's habitability law is short. For residential property you must deliver and keep the unit fit and habitable, meet applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes, make needed repairs, maintain the facilities and appliances you supply, keep common areas and garbage facilities in buildings with more than one unit, and supply water, hot water and heat to units on direct public utility connections. You are excused for conditions caused by the fault or lack of reasonable care of the tenant, the tenant's family or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent, and from repairs while the tenant is behind on rent, unless your lease promises more, because a greater lease duty controls. A tenant sued for unpaid rent may defend on your breach of a material covenant, and after a fire or other casualty not the tenant's fault rent is reduced and the tenant may leave if you do not rebuild in a reasonable time. Many rules found in other states are absent: no sentence making the duties non-waivable or allowing a waiver; no seriousness threshold or list of unfit conditions; no presumptions; no required habitability statement in the lease; no procedure for shifting duties to the tenant; no rule that repair promises be written or dated; no repair-request procedure or repair deadline; no repair-and-deduct, rent withholding, rent escrow or tenant termination for unmade repairs; no rule on who may make repairs; no right to end a lease because repairs cost too much; and no small-landlord exemption. Where those questions matter, the answer is case law, so take the cautious course: keep the duties, document requests and repairs, and do not rely on lease terms that reduce them.

title: Who Makes Repairs
bodyText:
No West Virginia statute gives a tenant a right to make repairs at your expense or deduct repair costs from rent, so there is no statutory procedure for naming who does that work. Your lease may name your repair contact and say the tenant will not make repairs at your cost, or deduct them from rent, without your written consent; the optional Repair Requests and Approved Repairers clause does that. Your habitability duties stay with you whoever does the work.

West Virginia's contractor licensing law generally requires a licensed contractor for residential work costing $5,000 or more, with exemptions that include work an owner or occupant performs personally on the structure, so name a licensed contractor when you approve larger jobs. Whether a contractor a tenant hires can claim a lien on your property, for example where you approved the work, is case law (see Liens for Work a Tenant Orders).

title: How Serious a Repair Problem Must Be
bodyText: West Virginia's habitability statute sets no seriousness threshold and lists no conditions that make a rental unfit. For residential property you must keep the unit fit and habitable, keep it in line with applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes, make all repairs needed to keep it fit and habitable, and keep the facilities and appliances you supply in good and safe working order. The statute does not leave out minor or cosmetic problems, and it does not define fit and habitable. Its only exceptions are a code violation caused by the fault of the tenant, a member of the tenant's family or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent, repairs needed mainly because one of them failed to take reasonable care, and repairs while the tenant is behind on rent (an excuse that a greater repair promise in your lease overrides). Seriousness matters in the eviction statute instead: in a summary eviction for unpaid rent, the court must hold a hearing if the tenant answers that you breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends. Code enforcement has its own tests: county and city ordinances may order the repair, closing or demolition of dwellings that are unfit for human habitation or unsafe, unsanitary or dangerous. How serious a defect must be before a court excuses rent or awards the tenant anything is case law, so treat every repair request as within your duty unless one of the statute's exceptions applies.

title: Changing the Repair Duties by Lease
bodyText:
West Virginia's habitability statute lets a lease change its duties in one direction only: if your rental agreement gives you a greater duty than the statute does, the agreement controls. No statute lets a lease reduce, waive or hand off the statutory duties, and none forbids it in words. Whether a court would enforce a reduction is case law, so do not rely on one.

Two duties turn partly on facts the lease can record. The facilities and appliances duty covers what you supply or must supply by written or oral agreement or by law, so a lease may list appliances you do not supply (this library's Appliances Not Supplied by Landlord clause). The running water, hot water and heat duty applies only to a unit supplied by direct public utility connections, and not where the unit is built so that its water, heat or hot water comes from an installation within the tenant's exclusive control. That limit comes from how the unit is served and built, not from a lease term, so a lease cannot switch the duty off.

The statute also does not require repairs while the tenant is behind on rent, but a lease that promises repairs with no such exception, as this library's Maintenance & Repairs clause does, gives up that excuse.

title: No Presumptions About Repairs
bodyText: No West Virginia statute creates a presumption about the condition of a rental: none presumes that a unit is or is not fit and habitable, that a housing code violation breaches your duty, that a repair problem was caused by the tenant, or that an eviction after a complaint is retaliation. In a summary eviction for unpaid rent, if the tenant answers that you breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends, the court must hold a hearing on that issue, and the statute does not say who must prove what. Your duty to keep the unit fit and habitable does not apply to code violations caused by the fault of the tenant, a member of the tenant's family or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent, or to repairs needed mainly because one of them did not take reasonable care, but the statute does not say who must prove that. Burdens of proof are case law, so keep dated records of the unit's condition at move-in and move-out, of repair requests and of the repairs you made.

title: No Required Habitability Statement
bodyText: No West Virginia statute or rule requires your lease to say that you will deliver or keep the unit fit and habitable, or to describe your repair duties. For residential property the habitability duties apply whether or not the lease mentions them: you must deliver the unit and surrounding premises fit and habitable at the start of the tenancy and keep them that way. What the lease does say matters, because a repair duty in the lease that is greater than the statute's controls. A broad maintenance promise therefore binds you beyond the statute, as this library's Maintenance & Repairs clause does by promising repairs with no exception for times when the tenant is behind on rent.

title: Waiving Habitability Requirements
bodyText: No West Virginia statute says whether a lease or other written agreement can remove a habitability requirement, such as the duty to keep the unit fit and habitable, meet housing codes, maintain supplied facilities or supply water, hot water and heat. The habitability statute has no sentence making its duties non-waivable, and none allowing a waiver. Its only rule about the lease runs the other way: if the lease gives you a greater duty than the statute, the lease controls. No statute lets a tenant accept a listed defect in exchange for lower rent, or requires a separate signed document for an agreement about heat. The one statutory rent reduction is the casualty rule: if buildings are destroyed or damaged by fire or otherwise without the tenant's fault or negligence, rent is reasonably reduced until they are replaced, unless the lease provides otherwise. Whether a court would enforce a waiver of the habitability duties is case law. The cautious course is not to rely on any lease term or side agreement that waives or reduces them, and this library's West Virginia lease offers none; if a unit has a known problem at move-in, repair it rather than asking the tenant to accept it.

title: Tenant Remedies When You Breach
